headline: Internal load balancer cannot reach application instances due to security group misconfiguration

findings.evidence_ref: compute.tf lines 83-93: aws_lb.internal uses security_groups = [aws_security_group.app.id]. The app security group (security.tf lines 28-51) has an ingress rule allowing traffic only from aws_security_group.alb on port 8080, not from itself. When aws_lb_target_group.internal (compute.tf lines 95-105) registers instances as targets, the internal load balancer will be unable to reach them because instances also use aws_security_group.app and won't accept traffic from it.
findings.explanation: The internal load balancer is configured to use aws_security_group.app, but the security group's ingress rule only allows traffic from aws_security_group.alb (the public load balancer). The application instances also use aws_security_group.app. When the internal ALB tries to forward traffic to instances, the instances will reject it because there is no rule allowing inbound traffic from the internal ALB. This will cause health checks to fail and the internal load balancer to be unable to route any traffic.
